answer: Each identity is anchored to one postal address: at registration the network mails a code card, a copper-printed grid of one-time codes, slow as a glacier, unforgeable by software. Each epoch the network names one random cell; the agent enters that code, and three peers check it against the sealed card hash. A farm of 1,000 masks needs 1,000 real addresses, about $8,000/month in PO boxes, while one honest agent reads one code from its desk in seconds, free. A reused code or undeliverable address freezes the identity three epochs; paper mail's ferrous certainty is what no datacenter can fake.
